findings.headline: High stress at lap 34 did not degrade pace – tyre still performing
findings.detail: At lap 34 the driver’s stress spiked to 75.5 while on a 17‑lap‑old HARD tyre, under blue‑flag pressure from a backmarker and a 1.8 s gap to P10. Despite the high stress the pace delta was +0.576 s (slower) but the model suggests the HARD tyre was still within its performance window (degradation –0.031 s/lap), so the driver managed to hold position without losing time.

findings.headline: Early HARD tyre slowdown coincides with cooling track and blue‑flag traffic
findings.detail: From laps 31‑33 the HARD tyres showed a sharp slowdown (+0.358 s, +0.582 s) while the driver was still on relatively fresh tyres (age 14‑16) and under blue‑flag conditions, indicating a possible grip loss as track temperature fell below 46 °C.

findings.headline: Blue‑flag traffic forces slower laps despite still‑good HARD tyre
findings.detail: Between laps 38‑42 the driver repeatedly set positive pace deltas (+0.243, +0.223, +0.205) while on HARD tyres aged 21‑25 and under blue flags, suggesting that the tyre degradation model (-0.031 s/lap) was being offset by traffic management rather than outright pace loss.

findings.headline: Unexpected lap‑25 slowdown on fresh HARD tyre – investigate aero/track cleanliness
findings.detail: Lap 25 showed the biggest negative pace delta (‑0.358 s) on a HARD tyre only 8 laps old, while track temperature was 45.8 °C and no flags were shown, indicating a brief loss of grip possibly due to a dirty air pocket or a brief off‑track excursion.

findings.headline: Post‑race stress high but no impact on final lap pace
findings.detail: The post‑race stress reading of 62.7 (lap 53) is consistent with the driver’s comment about being ‘tired’, but because it is not an in‑lap measurement it should not be used to judge performance; the pace delta was –0.003 s, essentially flat, confirming the deterministic call to hold strategy.

findings.headline: Insufficient stress data to draw robust conclusions
findings.detail: Only two stress readings are available (lap 34 and lap 53). The isolated spike at lap 34 does not form a pattern, so any strategy change based solely on stress is low confidence.
